Subject: Renewal discussion: reserved pool expansion and tokens/sec ask

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we approach our May renewal at Acumen, procurement has a few requests so we can finalize internal approval:

- We plan to increase our reserved pool by +4 A100-equivalent GPUs (estimated sustained workload).
- We need a firm tokens/sec commitment for the reserved pool with SLO language that maps to credits for missed throughput. Our primary workload is batch + low-latency interactive agents; target baseline is ~120k tokens/sec sustained with 240k burst for short windows.
- Please include fallback behavior: which model variants will be used if the primary capacity is constrained, and whether automatic routing to hosted spare capacity is included.
- We also need audit evidence (token-level throughput graphs, 30-day latency distribution) in the addendum for our internal security/compliance review.

Attached is a short RFP excerpt and our renewal timeline. Can you send a proposed addendum and an ops playbook for how Redwood will guarantee tokens/sec (and credits) during the committed term?

We prefer a May 1 start date for the additional reserved pool capacity.

Thanks,
Nadia Suresh
Head of Procurement
Acumen Robotics

Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: reserved pool expansion and tokens/sec ask

Nadia —

Appreciate the clarity and the timeline. Attached is a first-pass addendum and an ops runbook draft that maps the committed reserved pool to a tokens/sec SLO and crediting framework. Highlights:

- Committed capacity: +4 reserved GPUs (A100-equivalent) added to your existing pool, effective 2027-05-01 (aligned to renewal).
- Baseline throughput: 120,000 tokens/sec sustained across the reserved pool.
- Burst window: up to 240,000 tokens/sec for short bursts (aggregate across pool) with automated throttling to protect latency SLOs.
- Availability SLO: 99.5% of 1-minute tokens/sec measurement windows must meet >= 90% of the baseline throughput. Missed SLOs trigger service credits: 5% monthly credit for first breach, escalated per subsequent breach.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to a green-hosted fallback model variant (quantized) when per-region reserved pool utilization exceeds 95%. Fallbacks capped to maintain secrecy and cost controls; reduced throughput but preserved response semantics.
- Observability: token-level throughput graphs, 30/90-day latency percentiles, and an audit bundle delivered monthly via a secure link.

Please note the SLO uses a tokens/sec measurement computed at the serving runtime ingress (post-batching). We include an appendix describing measurement points and edge cases (cold start, model warm-up, KV cache priming).

Next steps: legal/finance redlines, then DocuSign for final execution. I’ve looped Marissa for billing and Laura for the SLO language review.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Apr 05, 2027 at 11:04, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> Please note the SLO uses a tokens/sec measurement computed at the serving runtime ingress (post-batching).

Quick clarifying notes from billing/ops:

- Billing model for the committed reserve will be a blended monthly reserved fee (GPU reserved capacity) + a committed tokens/sec surcharge that preserves price predictability. Overage pricing applies above the committed sustained baseline; overage will be metered per-minute and invoiced monthly.
- Credits for missed SLOs will be applied to the invoice in the following billing cycle; we will include examples in the addendum that show how credits are calculated (sample math).
- For the proposed automatic fallback to hosted quantized variants: fallback compute consumption will be billed at a reduced rate and will not count against the reserved token budget unless explicitly configured.

I'll work with Legal to tighten the SLO language around maintenance exclusions and force majeure windows. Laura — please confirm the wording on the 99.5% availability and the measurement window.

—Marissa

If you can accept those two items, we’ll route the DocuSign package today and target a May 1 activation. We attached a short forecast SOW for capacity phasing (you’ll see production ramp in weeks 2–6).
